newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mandela joins tribute to late Mozambican leader.
newsitem.headline: Mandela joins tribute to late Mozambican leader.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela joined his Mozambican companion Graca Machel this weekend to pay homage to President Samora Machel, her late husband, in the village where he was born.

The couple, who recently made public their romance, came to Chilembene in southern Mozambique to remember the man who led Mozambique to independence from Portugal in 1975 and died in a plane crash in South Africa in 1986.

"I am here to say thank you to the people and government of Mozambique and the Machel family for all the support you have given us," Mandela said in a speech at the five-hour ceremony of hymns, prayers and a sermon.
Graca has said she has "an amorous relationship" with Mandela but, still loyal to Machel, will not marry him.
It was Mandela's third tribute to Machel this month.
Last weekend, at a rally in the capital Maputo, he presented Graca with a posthumous medal for Samora Machel for his support in the struggle against apartheid.

He has also revisited the scene of the crash that killed Machel, on the South African side of the border, and vowed to find out what really happened. A report blamed pilot error but rumours of apartheid-era sabotage persist.

Mandela arrived at Chilembene, 150 km (90 miles) south of Maputo, by helicopter to join hundreds of friends and villagers in lauding a man who was a hero to many for his role in southern African liberation struggles.
Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni also flew in for the ceremony and paid tribute to Machel for training his guerrilla forces who toppled Ugandan dictator Idi Amin.
"I would not travel all the way here if it were not for something very precious. Samora is not only a hero here, he is a hero in Uganda," he said.
President Joaquim Chissano, Machel's successor who is rebuilding the country after 16 years of civil war, also came to the ceremony, which ended with a parachute display.
One parachute bore Machel's picture with the Portuguese slogan he made famous -- "A luta continua" (the struggle continues).
